messages:
maria: heads-up — grafana alerted on a drop in token-latency series for /api/v1/generate around 2026-02-14 07:03 UTC. looks like a hole of ~2h where token.* metrics went from 120k/min to ~0.

josh: ugh. did we redeploy anything to infra around that window?

exporter-bot: deploy event: runtime-service v3.8.1 -> v3.9.0 rolled at 2026-02-14T07:01:12Z (change: kernel-selection heuristics + kv-cache batching change).

anya: that matches. v3.9.0 included the KV-cache TTL flush change (we increased flush frequency to reduce memory spikes). suspect cardinality explosion hit the StatsD exporter.

maria: looking at the statsd-exporter logs, I see repeated "udp queue full, dropping metrics" and a ton of unique keys like token.latency.route:route_id:session:kv_keyhash. snippet: ```WARN exporter/statsd: dropping 3000 metrics/s (udp buffer full) key example=token.latency.route:gen:v2:kv_0x7f12a3```

josh: can you dump a small sample of keys? if kv_keyhash is leaking session ids we need to sanitize the exporter key template ASAP.

anya: attaching quick grep output (trimmed):
```
token.latency.route:chat:session:kv_0x7f12a3
token.latency.route:chat:session:kv_0x7f12a4
token.latency.route:chat:session:kv_0x7f12a5
... repeated with many session ids ...
```
This is new: before we aggregate by route+model+bucket, we accidentally included per-session hash in the metric name when KV cache restructure landed.

sam: timeline proposal: (1) hotfix exporter to drop/sanitize kv suffixes (2) backfill missing token-level metrics for dashboards (3) run audit to confirm no other metric names leaked.

maria: +1. hotfix PR already open: https://git.redwood/runtime/pulls/842 patch will truncate metric names to the canonical schema token.latency.route:{route_id}:{bucket}.

josh: for backfill — what raw sources can reconstruct token-level latency? we need per-route KPIs and token-level breakdowns (decode, kv-lookup, kernel, kernel-wait).

anya: traces (OTel) include span-level timing for kernel and kv operations. routing logs include request->route mapping and token counts. We can join traces + routing logs to compute token-level latencies per route. problem: some traces were also sampled low in that window. but we should be able to reconstruct most of the aggregate by combining:
- all traces (full traces stored for internal-sampled=1)
- runtime routing logs (high-volume append-only)
- request meta logs (contains model, route_id, session flags)

sam: backfill plan sketch:
1) run an exporter-scan job to identify all unique routes and time ranges with gaps (fast mapreduce).
2) for each route-range, join routing logs -> traces -> reconstruct token-level breakdown. output into metrics backfill aggregator which posts to graphite/metrics store with correct keys.
3) re-run dashboard rollup and mark the gap patched.
Estimate: 6-10 hours of cluster time for the 2-hour gap (IO heavy).

maria: any risk of double-counting once the hotfix deploys and normal exporter resumes? we need idempotent backfill writes.

josh: backfill writes should use a backfill tag in the metric stream and the metrics-aggregator will dedupe backfill writes if metric timestamp already exists (we track metric_version). I'll add a safety check.

anya: small profiling observation: the kernel selector change in v3.9.0 increased transient kernel-switch events which created an extra span per token in traces; that slightly bumps trace payload volume but nothing catastrophic. the real issue was the metric name change causing explosion.

maria: action items:
- anya: push exporter hotfix to canary in us-west in next 15m, monitor UDP-drop counters (ETA 20m).
- josh: schedule backfill job once hotfix is confirmed, add metric_version guard (ETA 1h to queue).
- sam: update dashboards to show backfill in legend and mark gap region.

sam: I'll also open a brief postmortem note in #incidents with timeline and root cause (metric-name leak due to KV-cache restructure + deploy).

josh: if the hotfix doesn't reduce dropped metrics, fallback is to switch statsd exporter to TCP proxy mode (slower but no UDP drops) while we do deeper fixes.

maria: monitoring: set alert if statsd_exporter_udp_drops > 1000/min for 10m post-deploy.

anya: FYI for runtime team: avoid including any per-session identifier or kv key hashes in metric names. use tags for that if needed (but preferably not).

maria: thanks everyone — I'll post updates here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
